subject.title: feat: add interactive launcher menu as thin wrapper over existing CLI

question: Should OpenClaw core own a new Rust interactive launcher menu, or should launch ergonomics stay in the existing CLI, onboarding, web, and native app surfaces for now?
rationale: The PR adds a new user-facing setup/startup surface and Rust build support while current project direction is terminal-first and warns against convenience wrappers that hide critical security decisions.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow launcher redesign
options.body: Keep the idea alive only if the branch is narrowed to launcher files, delegates configured readiness/version behavior, wires build/package support, and proves the real flows.

options.title: Decline core launcher for now
options.body: Close this PR and ask launch UX work to go through existing native app, onboarding, or a separate sponsored design proposal.

options.title: Accept the new surface deliberately
options.body: Maintain core Rust launcher support with explicit packaging, upgrade, and ownership commitments despite the added toolchain and support surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow launcher redesign
recommendation.body: Keep the idea alive only if the branch is narrowed to launcher files, delegates configured readiness/version behavior, wires build/package support, and proves the real flows.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest available product-direction and feature-history signal for setup, Gateway, TUI, and VISION.md direction.
